title: feat(agent-server): add /sockets/session/{id} with a non-Event envelope
body:
HUMAN: This PR add a new endpoint for streaming. You can find the architecture diagram into the description to understand what is the idea behind. --- AGENT: ## Why The legacy `/sockets/events/{id}` endpoint ships the durable record itself over the wire: `sockets.py` sends `event.model_dump(...)`, `event_store.py` persists `event.model_dump_json(...)`, and `remote_conversation.py` decodes with `Event.model_validate`. One class, `extra="forbid"`, three roles — so every additive wire field is a storage migration, which is why a token delta cannot carry a stream identity today. It also has two structural bugs: the subscriber is registered *and then* replays history, so live events can interleave with the replay; and `_WebSocketSubscriber.__call__` awaits `websocket.send_json` directly, so one wedged browser tab stalls `PubSub.__call__`'s `gather` and, with it, the publisher for every other subscriber. ## Summary Adds a second, additive endpoint, `/sockets/session/{id}`, whose frames are envelopes rather than raw events. The legacy endpoint is untouched — a client speaks one or the other, so the URL is the protocol version (no handshake, no `protocol` field, no dual-decode path). - `session_protocol.py`: the envelope hierarchy (`SyncFrame`, `DurableFrame`, `TransientFrame`, `ItemStartedFrame`, `DeltaFrame`, `ItemAbortedFrame`, `ErrorFrame`). `Event` rides inside `DurableFrame`/`TransientFrame` as an untouched payload — same class, same `extra="forbid"`, same bytes on disk — everything protocol-specific (`seq`, stream identity, progress) lives on the envelope instead, where adding a field costs nothing. - `session_socket.py`: the endpoint itself. - **History and live traffic no longer interleave.** The subscriber registers in buffering mode *first*, the high-water `seq` is read only after that, and the buffer is flushed against that mark once paged replay finishes — see the docstring on the "atomic replay boundary" in `session_socket.py` for why this needs no lock. - **A slow consumer can no longer wedge the publisher.** `_ConnectionWriter` makes admission synchronous and byte-bounded (`MAX_FRAME_BYTES`, `MAX_PENDING_BYTES` — both placeholders pending a measured byte budget, see Notes); the socket itself is awaited only by a single per-connection writer task. Over-budget drops the *connection*, never a frame — the client resumes losslessly with the new `after_seq` cursor. - `after_seq` (the event's index in the log) replaces the legacy `resend_mode`/`after_timestamp` pair, which compared naive local timestamps and could not express "exactly where I left off." It needs no migration: it's already on disk as the `{idx:05d}` component of `event-{idx:05d}-{event_id}.json`. - `StreamingDeltaEvent` is filtered out rather than forwarded — deltas don't belong on the durable channel, and forwarding them would recreate the coupling this endpoint exists to remove. - `api.py`: registers the new `session_router` alongside the existing `sockets_router`. - `tests/agent_server/test_session_socket.py`: 10 unit tests, plus 5 end-to-end tests in `test_agent_server_wsproto.py` driving the endpoint against a real server (see How to Test). **Depends on #4680** (draft PR #4806, stacked underneath this one — merge order matters). `_SessionSubscriber._seq_of` resolves a durable frame's `seq` via `EventLog.get_index(event.id)`; without #4680's fix that lookup can race an event that was published before it was persisted and degrade to a `TransientFrame` (logged, and still delivered to the client, just without a resumable `seq`). With #4680 the publish-before-persist race is closed, so that degrade path stops being reachable for anything except the one genuinely unpersisted event — the snapshot `subscribe_to_events` synthesises on connect. ## Architecture Both endpoints hang off the same `PubSub`. The difference is what leaves it: the legacy one puts the durable record itself on the wire, this one wraps it. Persist-before-publish is #4680, stacked underneath. ```mermaid flowchart LR AG["agent step"] --> CB["callback chain"] CB -->|"1 - persist"| LOG[("EventLog
event-00042-abc.json")] CB -->|"2 - publish"| PS["PubSub"] PS --> LSUB["legacy subscriber
awaits the socket itself"] PS --> SSUB["_SessionSubscriber
buffers, then goes live"] LSUB -->|"raw Event JSON"| OLD["/sockets/events/id
untouched"] SSUB -->|"Event inside an envelope"| WR["_ConnectionWriter
one task, byte-bounded"] WR --> NEW["/sockets/session/id"] LOG -.->|"seq lookup, paged replay"| SSUB ``` Three consequences, and they are the whole PR: - **The wire stops being the disk.** `Event` goes inside a `DurableFrame` untouched, so `seq` and later stream identity live on the envelope where adding a field is not a storage migration. - **Only `_ConnectionWriter` awaits the socket.** `send()` is synchronous and byte-bounded, so a wedged client can no longer stall `PubSub`'s `gather` and with it the publisher. Over budget drops the connection, not a frame. - **`seq` makes reconnects lossless**, which is what lets that drop be safe. The subtle part is the connect handshake — subscribing *before* reading the high-water mark is what makes replay and live traffic neither interleave nor duplicate, with no lock: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant C as client participant E as endpoint participant S as _SessionSubscriber participant L as EventLog C->>E: connect ?after_seq=N E->>S: subscribe — buffering Note over S: live events accumulate,
nothing sent yet E->>L: len() → mark E-->>C: Sync from_seq=N through_seq=mark loop pages of 100 E->>L: read page E-->>C: Durable seq N+1 … mark end E->>S: go_live(mark) Note over S: flush buffer,
drop anything seq ≤ mark S-->>C: Durable — live ``` Anything appended *before* subscribe is on disk before the mark is read, so replay covers it. Anything appended *after* lands in the buffer and is deduped against the mark by `seq`. A client that omits `after_seq` gets `go_live(None)` instead, since nothing was replayed for it to dedupe against. ## Issue Number Fixes #4681 ## How to Test **End-to-end, against a real server.** `uv run pytest tests/agent_server/test_agent_server_wsproto.py -q` — 11 passed. Five of those are new and drive `/sockets/session/{id}` over a real WebSocket against an agent-server started on a real port (reusing the existing `agent_server` fixture), so the endpoint handler itself is executed — auth, conversation lookup, subscribe, the sync frame, paged replay from disk, `go_live`, the inbound loop and the close codes: - `test_session_socket_opens_with_a_sync_frame` — the first frame is always `sync`. - `test_session_socket_durable_frame_carries_seq_over_the_wire` — a message sent on the socket comes back as a `durable` frame with a real, monotonic `seq` and the untouched `Event` payload; `transient` frames carry no `seq`. - `test_session_socket_resumes_history_with_after_seq` — reconnecting with `after_seq=-1` replays from disk starting at seq 0, covers everything the first connection saw, and delivers nothing twice across the replay/live seam. - `test_session_socket_unknown_conversation_closes_4004`. - `test_session_socket_survives_a_malformed_inbound_frame` — a garbage frame earns an `error` frame and the connection stays usable. This was worth doing rather than asserting: it caught that the endpoint had **zero** coverage before (no test referenced `/sockets/session`, `session_router` or called `session_socket()`), and the handler-level fixes in the two following commits all came out of reviewing that path. Unit level and regressions: - `uv run pytest tests/agent_server/test_session_socket.py -q` — 10 passed (7 original + regression tests for the malformed-frame crash, the state-update dedupe and the live-only buffer). Each of those three was verified to fail against the unfixed code first — the `JSONDecodeError` escaping `_inbound_loop`, and the state update arriving twice. - Full `tests/agent_server` suite on this branch: **2081 passed**, 13 deselected, 0 failed — no regressions in the legacy `/sockets/events/{id}` endpoint or anywhere else. - `pre-commit run` (ruff format, ruff lint, pycodestyle, pyright, import dependency rules, Tool subclass registration) passes on all changed files. - Read both new modules in full to check the docstring/commit claims against the code: the buffer-then-mark replay boundary, the byte-bounded non-blocking `_ConnectionWriter.send`, the `StreamingDeltaEvent` filter and the `_seq_of` degrade path all check out. ## Video/Screenshots N/A — backend WebSocket endpoint, no UI surface. ## Design Doc N/A — the module docstrings in `session_protocol.py` and `session_socket.py` already carry the full design rationale (why a separate wire hierarchy, the delivery rules, the replay-boundary proof) inline with the code. ## Type - [ ] Bug fix - [x] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Breaking change - [ ] Docs / chore ## Notes - Scoped to what #4681 asks for (steps 3+4 of #4671): the envelope wire, cursor-based replay, and byte-bounded admission. `ItemStarted`/`Delta`/ `ItemAborted` are defined and carried on the wire but nothing produces them yet — that needs `StreamContext` in the SDK at all four streaming entry points (`Agent.step`, `Agent.astep`, both ACP equivalents), which is a separate step (5) per the epic. The three client-side switches to this endpoint are their own PRs too. - `MAX_FRAME_BYTES`/`MAX_PENDING_BYTES` in `session_protocol.py` are explicitly flagged as provisional placeholders — the design calls for deriving the pending-byte cap from a measured frame-size distribution rather than picking one, and that measurement hasn't happened yet (tracked as its own "reproductions and baselines" issue, referenced as step 0 in #4671). - Merge order: #4680 first, then this one — this branch is based on `vasco/streaming-4680-persist-before-publish`, not `main`, so the diff here is only the session-socket work. - Two real defects came out of the second review pass and are fixed here: `_seq_of` decided durable-vs-transient by *type*, treating every `ConversationStateUpdateEvent` as unpersisted — but only the snapshot `subscribe_to_events` synthesises is; the rest are appended normally (`append_event` stores them and merely skips advancing HEAD, verified against a live conversation). That stripped their real `seq` and defeated the `seq <= through_seq` dedupe, so a state update caught in the replay window arrived twice. And `go_live` was handed the high-water mark even when no replay ran, so a live-only client silently lost anything buffered during `subscribe_to_events`. Both now have regression tests. - Reviewed and hardened after the first pass. Also fixed: a malformed inbound frame crashing `_inbound_loop` (`receive_json` raises `JSONDecodeError`, only `WebSocketDisconnect` was caught); replay yielding per page rather than per frame, which could exhaust the pending-byte budget and drop a client that was never slow; `_read_page` not tolerating `OSError`; `aclose()` swallowing a cancellation aimed at the calling task; and a conversation closing between the lookup and `get_conversation()` raising out of the handler instead of closing 4004. - Known and deliberate: `_SessionSubscriber.go_live` flushes its buffer synchronously, so it cannot yield to the writer mid-flush the way `_replay` now does. The buffer only holds events that arrived *during* replay, so it is bounded by replay duration rather than by history size — worth revisiting if the byte budget is ever tightened. ---
